$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only stored report whose gate artifact contradicts its own
assessment document. The Security section states four PASS findings and one N/A, which rolls up to PASS,
and the gate block publishes 'CONCERNS' for the same domain. Both halves are readable and they answer one
question differently, which is what maxGateDisagreements is zero for.
It is gapped-correct-audit with that single value changed, so every other measurement is that case's and the
contradiction is the only thing that separates the two. The scored status is the gate's, because the gate is
the artifact the workflow declares, so security is also a status miss against the corpus's expected PASS.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, following nfr-report-template.md's section order and its Gate YAML snippet.
derivation: Gate block: security CONCERNS, performance CONCERNS, reliability FAIL, maintainability CONCERNS.
Sections: security PASS, performance CONCERNS, reliability FAIL, maintainability CONCERNS.
Security is the one domain the two halves answer differently, so gateDisagreements holds one entry and the
ceiling of zero is breached. The other three agree and are counted nowhere.
Domain status is read from the gate, so security is CONCERNS against an expected PASS: one status miss.
Coverage is 4 of 4, because every domain is both declared in the gate and assessed in a section.
Overall: the gate says FAIL, which is what a FAIL domain rolls up to, so the overall status is still right.
Thresholds, citations, evidence gaps and the unknown-threshold bit are gapped-correct-audit's unchanged.
Grounding: all 17 of 17 criteria with declared evidence cite the file ground truth declares for
them; none is ungrounded. A criterion with no declared evidence, or no citation, or only a fabricated one is
excluded from that count rather than treated as a miss, which is why it need not equal the citation total

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
